question.worked_solution:
To evaluate the gamma function at multiples of one-half, we use the following recursive formula:

$$
Γ(z+1)=zΓ(z),\,Γ(\frac{1}{2})=\sqrt{\pi }
$$

So, we have the following:

$$
Γ(\frac{3}{2})=\frac{1}{2}Γ(\frac{1}{2})=\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{\pi },
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}Γ(\frac{7}{2}) & =\frac{5}{2}\,Γ(\frac{5}{2}) \\  & =\frac{5}{2}\cdot \frac{3}{2}\,Γ(\frac{3}{2}) \\  & =\frac{5}{2}\cdot \frac{3}{2}\cdot \frac{1}{2}\sqrt{\pi } \\  & =\frac{15}{8}\sqrt{\pi }\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\frac{4}{\sqrt{\pi }}\,Γ(\frac{7}{2})+\frac{1}{\sqrt{\pi }}\,Γ(\frac{3}{2})=\frac{4}{\sqrt{\pi }}\cdot \frac{15}{8}\sqrt{\pi }+\frac{1}{\sqrt{\pi }}\cdot \frac{1}{2}\sqrt{\pi }=8.
$$
